favourite.heading: Why Miami can pull away
bullets: Miami is the better football team by 27.5 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+27.5 pts).
Playing at Miami is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 4.0 points to Miami (+4.0 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Miami by 3.9 points: ball control vs front disruption (+3.9 pts).
Pass offense: Miami 67.9 (#2 of 132) vs Central Michigan 36.1 (#128 of 132) — 126 places on the national board.

underdog.heading: Why Central Michigan can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 +16.6 to p90 +60.6 for Miami, so a projection of +39.6 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
